title: i7b: teardown integrity scenario
description: test: teardown integrity. Bar set by RD6: PASS when (a) every entity we created is gone (registry emptied, verified by Shared.GetEntity(id) == nil polling), (b) BotTeamController lock released and state restored (EnableUpdate depth tracked, SetMaxBots from snapshot), (c) no horde state remains in gamerules/team tables, and (d) the before/after diff is logged and surfaced by sh_horde_status. An exact global entity-count delta is REPORTED as a signal, not asserted as a gate - vanilla churn during a run makes it flaky, and a flaky integrity gate gets ignored. If the global delta shows a leak we did not create, record it as a bug, do not weaken (a).

title: i0f: SPIKE - marine PlayerBot as hordetest fake player (RD5)
description: Prove marine PlayerBots can be spawned as fake players inside hordetest before i6c/i8b rely on them. Steps: spawn a marine bot on team 1 (PlayerBot recipe); determine whether a marine bot counts toward humanCount at BotTeamController.lua:172 (if not, tests must lock BTC); wrap with DisableUpdate + SetMaxBots snapshot/restore; verify clean Disconnect teardown with no slot leak. Decide: marine bots in tests (i6c/i8b then exercise real combat and a real wipe) or predicate-only fallback (headline loss condition stays untested headless).
close_reason: ANSWERED (live, build 344, commit 28d9a81): YES - marine PlayerBots work as headless test actors. Initialize(kTeam1Index,true) yields a live Marine player 6s later; GetPlayerNumbersForTeam(team,true) stays 0, so bots never count as humans and MinPlayers/wipe-loss stay truthful with bots on the field. TRAP: humanCount==0 makes BotTeamController:UpdateBots wipe all bots (BTC:169-172), so tests must DisableUpdate()+SetMaxBots(0) and restore. Added Plugin:Defer + runner now withholds ALL-DONE until deferred items land. Kept as standing regressions: spike_bot_players + spike_bot_resolves. Unlocks i6c and i8b for real combat/wipe tests.

title: i2a0: SPIKE - does the vanilla command chair work during WarmUp? (RD7)
description: Plan D6 parked this at M8; the build phase is a pillar (Q4/Q18) so it must be known before i2b. Check on build 344 source + headless: can a player enter the command chair while kGameState is WarmUp, do structures/upgrades buy, does the eject cycle behave, and does chair-mediated spending gate correctly? Outcome picks one: vanilla chair spending works (keep D6), chair is inert (build our own build-phase gate), or cut chair spending from the slice and shrink what the slice claims to prove.
close_reason: ANSWERED (live, build 344): YES - CommandStructure:LoginPlayer(player,true) succeeds during kGameState.WarmUp and leaves team:GetHasCommander() true (same call CommanderBot:119-127 uses). Plan D6 risk closed favourably: the marine build phase needs no custom chair gate, so Q4/Q17/Q18 stay as designed. Asserted permanently in spike_bot_resolves. NEW PROBLEM found while verifying: NS2Gamerules:GetAllTech() (1930-1932) returns true whenever state==WarmUp, and TechTree_Server:694-697 makes ALL tech available - undercutting Q5 (vanilla upgrade ladder) and Q13 (composition cadence via evolution gating). Not fixable by SetAllTech(false) in WarmUp. Needs Arian: option (c) accept all-tech + cost/time-only economy vs (a) patch tech availability for the horde window. Filed in vault research/td-spike-bot-players-and-warmup-chair.md.

Live evidence: alien bot spawned under the lock survived to t+15 with a live player on a zero-human server (the humanCount==0 wipe at :169-172 is held off), and cap + both commander flags restored exactly; Release writes the commander fields directly because SetMaxBots would assign one value to both (:185-193). Lock helpers encode verified engine facts: updateLock is a counted lock with an assert against unbalanced release (:140-147), and SetMaxBots(0) wipes ALL bots while assigning one com value to both commander fields (:185-193) - so release restores the flags directly and the cap change is a separate explicit step. title: i1b: config module — DefaultConfig + validators + Maps deep-merge
description: feat: config module. Scope updated by RD4: curves are built in Phase 1, end to end, so DefaultConfig carries a curve set (Start, End, Bezier control points) for EVERY scaled quantity - wave composition, bot HP/armor/damage, mouth band, wave payout, and per RD2 the accuracy and aggro levers (absent = vanilla defaults). Not a flat number table. Constraints: BandMin must respect the spike measurement (summit reachable starts around 56m, not the old 20m); every endpoint shipped before Arians balance session (RD3) is commented "untuned, placeholder 2026-09-20"; Maps deep-merge convention kept; Validator rejects non-positive numbers, inverted bands, and malformed curve sets. Tests: config scenarios - defaults load, deep-merge override wins, bad value falls back and notifies, curve set evaluates monotonically over the wave range.
close_reason: Done in this commit. All placeholders marked untuned pending RD3; curves ship disabled so untuned data cannot change behaviour. RD8 applied: no tech-gating fields in the schema (WarmUp grants all tech; cost and time are the only constraints). Two bugs caught by the new scenarios on first live run: Assert.Equal arg convention mismatched every call site (failures reported expected/got backwards), and bisection never reaching t=0/1 made wave 1 = 4.000000179 bots - endpoints now exact and short-circuited. Verified live: pass=11 fail=0 expected_fail=1, exit 0.

Also fixed a genuine load-path defect found by these tests: Plugin.HasConfig was never set (Shine skips LoadConfig without it, extensions.lua:656), and setting it alone crashed the extension because ConfigName is concatenated unguarded (base_plugin/config.lua:32) - now HasConfig=true + ConfigName="HordeMode.json". Verified: verified accessor NS2Gamerules:GetGameState() (:171) and kGameState enum (Globals.lua:265). Harness regressions hordemode_armed + hordemode_arms_once pass live (ALL-DONE pass=6 fail=0 expected_fail=1, exit 0). Test wording said assert no-errors-since-boot; that helper is unimplemented (no verified hook), so the scenario asserts loaded+armed+poll-retired instead, and test.sh surfaces log errors as diagnostics.

title: i0d: hordetest scenario framework
description: hordetest extension: scenario table (name, fn, order), runner timer gated on world-ready + 10s settle, assert helpers (AssertTrue/AssertEq/AssertNotNil/AssertAlive/AssertGone/AssertNoErrors since boot), [TEST] <name> PASS|FAIL <detail> logging, final [TEST] ALL-DONE pass=N fail=M. Ship with: world_ready PASS scenario + demo_fail scenario (behind config flag, default off) proving FAIL detection + exit-code propagation through test.sh.
close_reason: Done in the i0d commit. DEVIATION 1: the demo failure ships as an always-on negative control (Expected=true) rather than a config-flagged demo_fail — a flag that defaults off proves FAIL detection only when someone remembers to flip it, and Shine's per-extension config file naming is unverified, so no config dependency was invented. DEVIATION 2: assert helpers are Plugin.Assert.{True,Equal,NotNil,Alive,Gone} instead of AssertTrue/AssertEq/..., and AssertNoErrorsSinceBoot is deliberately NOT implemented — a global "no lua errors since boot" check needs an unverified hook, so it stays a spike rather than a fake assertion. Verified live: ALL-DONE pass=2 fail=0 expected_fail=1 -> exit 0; the negative control FAILs as designed; a greedy-parse bug (.*fail= matching expected_fail) was caught by the first real run, fixed with an anchored pattern plus an unparseable-line guard.

title: Decide horde-mode <-> vanilla WarmUp/filler-bot interaction
description: Build 344 ships a vanilla WarmUp seeding mode: below 12 humans it fills both teams with filler bots (BotTeamController, config filler_bots=12) and spawns warmup structures. This is the SAME window horde mode targets. Decide: on /horde, suppress vanilla BotTeamController (SetMaxBots(0)+DisableUpdate) and run only our horde bots, restore on teardown (LEAN). Also: teardown filter must distinguish OUR bots from vanilla filler bots (track in HordeRegistry, never teardown-trigger on any virtual join). Verify WarmUp doesn't auto-start a real round without commanders. See vault research/td-vanilla-warmup-and-bot-framework.md §6.
